la:noun:ibis.html:
ībis, is and ĭdis (
nom. plur. ibes, ; ; gen. ibium, ; gen. sing. ibidis, ; acc. plur. ibidas, fin.; acc. sing. ibim, ; ; : ibin,; ), f., = ἶβις, a bird held sacred by the Egyptians, and which lived on water-animals, the ibis: Numenius ibis, Cuv.; ; ; ; ; .—
Transf., Ibis, the title of a satiric poem by Ovid (after Callimachus, who bestowed the name of Ibis on Apollonius of Rhodes).

la:adv:ibidem.gloss: in that very place; in or at the same place; in, at, or on the same spot
senses: in that very place; in or at the same place; in, at, or on the same spot
at that very instant, at the same time
la:adv:ibidem.html:
ĭbīdem (always ĭbĭdem in Plaut.;
v.infra; so ; ), adv.
ibi, with demonstr. suff. dem, as in idem, tandem, tantundem, etc.
, in the same place, in that very place, just there.
Lit., in space: sarmenta concidito minute et ibidem inarato,: cenati discubuerunt ibidem,: ille, cujus merces erant, in gladium ibidem incumberet,: quod ibidem recte custodire poterunt, id ibidem custodiant,: ne hīc ibidem ante oculos vestros trucidetur,: ego ibidem has inter cenam exaravi, i. e. on the spot, immediately, id. Fragm. ap. : cum ibidem invenire fingimus, Spald. N. cr.; cf. ibi, I.: pede terram Crebra ferit: demissae aures, incertus ibidem Sudor, i. e. circa aures,.—With a corresp. ubi: ubi amici, ibidem opes,: ibidem divitiarum cupido est, ubi et usus,.—With gen.: si redierit Illa ad hunc, ibidem loci res erit,.—With a verb of motion (for eodem): egomet me cum illis una ibidem traho,I reckon myself among them, on the same plane with them,: St. Quid, quod dedisti scortis? Le. Ibidem una traho, to that very account, .—
Transf.
Of time, in that very moment (= paene eodem temporis momento): Deinde ibidem homo acutus, cum illud occurreret, Madv.; so, deinde ibidem,; cf.: ibidem ilico puer abs te cum epistulis,.—
Of other relations, in the same matter: tibi ibidem das. ubi tu tuom amicum adjuvas,: laesit in eo Caecinam, sublevavit ibidem, i. e. in eo ipso,: tibi non committitur aurum, vel si quando datur, custos affixus ibidem,.

la:adv:ibi.html:
ĭbĭ_, adv.
from the pronom. root I, is, with dat. ending as in tibi, sibi, in loc. sense as in ubi; cf. Sanscr. suffix bhjam; Corss. Ausspr. 1, 169
,
in that place, there, = ἐνταῦθα (cf. istic).
Lit., in space: ibi cenavi atque ibi quievi in navi noctem perpetem,; tandem abii ad praetorem. Ibi vix requievi,: nempe in foro? De. Ibi, : in Asiam hinc abii, atque ibi, etc.,: Demaratus fugit Tarquinios Corintho et ibi suas fortunas constituit,; : aedificabat in summa Velia: ibi alto atque munito loco arcem inexpugnabilem fore,: erit haec differentia inter hoc edictum et superius, quod ibi de eo damno praetor loquitur, etc.,: musca est meus pater ... nec sacrum nec tam profanum quicquamst, quin ibi ilico adsit,: ut illa, quae dicimus, non domo attulisse, sed ibi protinus sumpsisse videamur,there, on the spot,; ; : in eo flumine pons erat. Ibi praesidium ponit,.—In common speech, sometimes pleonastic, with the name of a place: in medio propter canalem, ibi ostentatores meri,; ; ; ; cf.: illic ibi demum'st locus, ubi, etc.,.—With corresp. relative adverbs, ubi, unde, etc.: nam ubi tu profusus, ibi ego me pervelim sepultam,: nemo est, quin ubivis quam ibi, ubi est, esse malit,; cf.: ibi esse, ubi, etc.,: ubi tyrannus est, ibi ... dicendum est plane nullam esse rem publicam,: multa intelleges meliora apud nos multo esse facta quam ibi fuissent, unde huc translata essent,.—So with quo loco, etc.: quo loco maxime umor intus perseverabit, ibi pus proximum erit,; cf.: quacumque equo invectus est, ibi haud secus quam pestifero sidere icti pavebant,: quo descenderant, ibi processerunt longe,.—With gen.: ibi loci terrarum orbe portis discluso,.—Post-class. of vessels, etc., therein (= in eis): qui sciens vasa vitiosa commodavit, si ibi infusum vinum est, etc.,.—Post-class. and very rarely with verbs of motion (for eo): et cum ibi venerimus,there, thither,; cf. ibidem.—
Transf.
Of time, then, thereupon (mostly ante - class. and poet., but freq. in Liv.): invocat deos inmortales: ibi continuo contonat Sonitu maxumo, etc.,; cf.: ubi ... ibi,: postquam ... ibi,: ter conatus ibi collo dare bracchia circum,: ibi infit, etc.,: nec moram ullam, quin ducat, dari: Ibi demum ita aegre tulit, ut, etc.,then for the first time,: ibi postquam laborare aciem Calpurnius vidit, Liv. 39, 31, 4.—With cum: ibi cum alii mores et instituta eorum eluderent,: ibi cum de re publica retulisset,.—With corresp. ubi: ille ubi miser famelicus videt, me tam facile victum quaerere, ibi homo coepit me obsecrare, etc.,: non voco (te patrem): Ubi voles pater esse, ibi esto,.—Pleonastically with tum: tum ibi nescio quis me arripit,: ibi tum derepente ex alto in altum despexit mare, Enn. ap. (Trag. Rel. v. 352 Vahl.): cum Aebutius Caecinae malum minaretur, ibi tum Caecinam postulasse, etc.,; cf.: ibi nunc (colloq.),; .—
Of other relations, there, in that matter, on that occasion, in that condition (class.): nolite ibi nimiam spem habere, Cato ap. : numquid ego ibi peccavi?: at pol ego ibi sum, esse ubi miserum hominem decet,: si quid est, quod ad testes reservet, ibi nos quoque paratiores reperiet,: ibi fortunae veniam damus,in that case,: huic ab adulescentia bella intestina, caedes, rapinae, discordia civilis grata fuere, ibique juventutem suam exercuit,in these things,; : non poterat ibi esse quaestio,: subsensi illos ibi esse et id agere inter se clanculum,to be at it, busy about it,: ibi esse,; cf.: cecinere vates, cujus civitatis eam civis Dianae immolasset, ibi fore imperium,i. e. in that state,: ibi imperium fore, unde victoria fuerit,: et interdum in sanctionibus adicitur, ut qui ibi aliquid commisit, capite puniatur, i. e. in his sanctionibus,.—
Of persons, in or with him or her (very rare): duxi uxorem; quam ibi miseriam vidi! (cf.: ibi inquit, quasi uxor locus sit, Don. ad loc.); cf.: nil ibi majorum respectus,.—
Esp., law t. t.: tunc ibi, then and there, in the state of affairs then existing: de eo, quaque ille tunc ibi habuit, tantummodo, intra annum ... judicium dabo,; cf.: ibi autem ait praetor, ut ne quis et quae illic non habuit, complectatur, ib. § 37 sq.
